hook: A U.S. Air Force ISR aircraft (50th Attack Squadron, 432nd AEW) flying a 20.5-hour reconnaissance mission over the Eastern Mediterranean on May 29-30, 2022 filed both a UAP report and conventional intelligence observations documenting extensive Russian military activity near the Syrian coast, including naval vessels, aircraft, and a separate SU-27/35 landing at the Latakia airfield area.
why_it_matters: This document illustrates that the UAP sighting occurred in a heavily contested operational environment where Russian forces were actively present—including a likely SU-27/35 landing and takeoff roughly one hour before the UAP contact—yet the screener still could not obtain a positive identification on the 0117Z object. The report demonstrates AARO's intake of operationally-filed UAP events rather than dedicated UAP investigations, and the Five Eyes classification indicates allied intelligence sharing of this event. The co-presence of identified Russian aircraft and an unidentified object in the same airspace within the same mission window is the core ambiguity the document leaves unresolved.
key_findings: At 0117Z on May 30, 2022, one UAP was observed flying north to northeast at FL240, 142 KIAS; the screener tracked it as long as possible but could not obtain a positive identification—no shape, size, color, or RF signatures are recorded in the unredacted text.

Approximately one hour earlier (0011Z), the same asset separately observed a 'probable SU-27/35' landing near grid 36SYE6 (consistent with Bassel al-Assad International Airport, Latakia), and at 0029Z observed a probable SU-27/35 taking off to the south—these are filed under OBSERVATION, not the UAP section.

The U.S. aircraft was intercepted at 2147Z by 1-3 Russian Air Force aircraft, including at least one possible SU-30, which approached from the Syrian coast, flew directly under the U.S. aircraft's orbit (FL190 vs FL240), flew south 10 NM, then returned west; there was no impact to the mission.

The mission surveilled 39 named targets across Syria and Lebanon including Tartus Naval Base, Latakia Naval HQ, multiple Syrian Navy coastal defense sites, and the Bassel al-Assad airfield, and observed Russian naval vessels including a Slava-class cruiser, a Gorshkov-class frigate, and two Udaloy I-class destroyers transiting east.

Russian aircraft parked at Latakia were identified as one A-50U Mainstay AEW aircraft and two IL-38 maritime patrol aircraft, plus a probable IL-76 transport active at 0006Z—placing the UAP sighting in an environment with confirmed, identified Russian military air activity minutes prior.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The mission report was explicitly submitted to AARO and declassified under MDR 25-0094 through 25-0099 for release to AARO, making this a primary AARO intake document.
The document is classified SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY throughout, indicating the UAP event and associated ISR intelligence were shared across the Five Eyes partnership.

The mission collected SIGINT via airhandler and IMINT (FMV exploited by DGS-1N and DGS4), suggesting coordination with national-level imagery and signals exploitation infrastructure, though no NRO entity is named directly.
